- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative or mixed (≤0.5), model often underestimates; increase forecast to reflect risk/reversal.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a downward correction of 2–5%.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model may lag; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% in the following 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion is common in 10–15 day windows; if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3%.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture late-stage momentum; add 1–3% upward bias if sentiment is bullish in last 5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to be flat; add 0.5–2% upward bias to account for hidden volatility.
